`CHANGELOG.md`:

```md
# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- `-Depth16:off` and `-Depth16:on`, scd3d11's name for `-DepthBuffer:32` and `16`
- `-borderless:off` and `-b:off` keep the window mode in the game's options instead of the borderless default
- `scvk.log` names the `scvk.ini` it read, or says there is none, and says when no `MaxFPS` is set
- `scvk.log` shows the game's command line
- `scvk.dll` carries its version and description, which Windows shows on the file's Details tab
- In borderless and fullscreen the cursor stays on the main monitor while the game is in front

### Changed

- Launch options that turn something on or off also take `true`, `false`, `enabled`, `disabled`, `1` and `0`, as in scd3d11, and mean on by themselves
- `scvk.log` and the setup dialog show the Windows account in paths as `%USERPROFILE%` or `%USERNAME%`
- With live shadows off, the default, scvk no longer hooks the game's static city view for them

### Fixed

- The city scrolls at the screen's edges in borderless, as it does in exclusive fullscreen
- The Rhino speed cap follows the others again. scvk read it one byte off, took the 0 there for another plugin's change, logged it as `Rhino 0` and left the game's 20

## [0.5.0] - 2026-11-01

### Added

- Setup checks at startup, which write to `scvk.log`: another driver drawing, any plugin loaded twice, SC4RenderServices older than 0.8.3, plugins built for SC4RenderServices before 0.8, plugins missing the Visual C++ runtime, no 4GB patch, compatibility mode, launch switch and `scvk.ini` typos, an unquoted `-UserDir` and unreadable lines in `SC4GraphicsOptions.ini`
- Serious setup problems also show in the game's own dialog when the region view opens. `DoctorDialog=false` in `scvk.ini` or `-DoctorDialog:off` keeps them in the log
- `scvk.log` names each graphics card's driver version and video memory, every DLL loaded with its version, and free address space, RAM and commit at startup and when an allocation fails
- `-GPU:<n>` picks a graphics card by its number in `scvk.log`, and scvk warns when a much faster card sits idle
- `-DepthBuffer:32` and `-DepthBuffer:16` launch options, ahead of `Use32BitDepth` in `scvk.ini`
- `-LiveShadows:on` and `-LiveShadows:off`, the name scd3d11 uses now, the same as `-NativeShadowMasks:replace` and `off`
- `-d:Vulkan` picks scvk for a launch, whatever scd3d11 or `Driver=` in `SC4GraphicsOptions.ini` would choose
- The setup checks tell a plugin that is a debug build from one missing the Visual C++ runtime, since only Visual Studio has what a debug build needs
- `scvk.log` notes a depth offset other than 0, the first time each one is asked for

### Changed

- Scrolling is lighter: draws wholly outside the strip the game is redrawing are left out before their vertices are copied. `-ViewportCull:off` sends them all, as before
- Less work around each draw when the game repeats a matrix or texture setting it already made
- scvk stays out of the way when it isn't the renderer. With scd3d11 or the Software driver drawing, it doesn't start Vulkan, patch the game, install its fault log, change the video mode or show its setup dialog
- One Vulkan instance less at startup, since the slot the game does not use no longer makes one

### Fixed

- After a lost graphics device the game is asked to upload its textures again, as its DirectX driver does
- A stalled graphics card no longer hangs the game while it saves, takes a photo or uploads textures. That read or upload is skipped instead
- A comment after a value in `scvk.ini`, such as `Use32BitDepth=true ; note`, no longer stops the value being read
- Live shadows redraw when a camera plugin changes the yaw or pitch
- Live shadows no longer force a full redraw on every scroll frame along the city's edge
- Live shadows no longer shade the backdrop beyond the city

## [0.4.0] - 2026-10-31

### Added

- A stencil buffer, so SC4RenderServices 0.8.3 or newer draws terrain decals back over shadows once per pixel and overlapping decals no longer come out darker

### Changed

- Cards without a 16-bit depth format that has a stencil use a 24-bit or 32-bit one, with every depth rounded to 16 bits
- The zip has a `scvk.ini` again, for anyone who wants to change a setting such as `Use32BitDepth`. scvk still runs without it

## [0.3.0] - 2026-10-28

Most of this release is UlisseWolf's port of scd3d11's features.

### Added

- ReShade's effects draw under the interface, with the city's depth, when ReShade is installed with full add-on support. `-ReShade:off` leaves it drawing over everything
- Live shadows for True3D props and network pieces, off by default. `-NativeShadowMasks:all` turns them on, and `-NativeShadowMasks:replace` adds the experimental shadow registry and terrain shadows
- PrintScreen in exclusive fullscreen puts the game's own picture on the clipboard, instead of opening the Snipping Tool and dropping the game out of fullscreen
- Region thumbnails no longer go blank when the game loses focus while saving
- `-MaxFPS:<n>` and `-MaxFPS:off` for the speed caps, ahead of `MaxFPS` in `scvk.ini`
- scd3d11's launch options: `-VSync:off`, `-GPU:default`, `-FlipModel:off`, `-LogLevel:<level>` and `-FullscreenMode:Borderless`
- `-b` and `-borderless` launch options for a borderless window, which sc4-graphics-options' borderless mode gives too
- `-windowed` and `-fullscreen` launch options, the same as `-w` and `-f`
- A pipeline cache beside the DLL, so later sessions build their pipelines faster
- A watchdog and fault reports in `scvk.log`, which say where a frozen or crashed game was
- The log notes Wine and its version when the game runs on Linux
- A MinGW build and a Wine test harness, for building and testing on Linux

### Changed

- The game starts borderless, in a frameless window covering the main monitor at the desktop's size. `-w`, `-f` or a `-r` size pick another mode, and sc4-graphics-options' settings still decide when it is installed
- The game runs in 32-bit colour even when its options or `-r` ask for 16, which made its textures band
- A `-r` size is used as given, without needing `-CustomResolution:enabled`. `-CustomResolution:disabled` keeps the game's own size
- With sc4-graphics-options installed, its settings still decide both
- The speed caps follow the display's refresh rate. A `scvk.ini` from 0.2, which says `MaxFPS=0`, keeps the game's caps
- Faster scrolling, with 13 to 21% more frames a second in the benchmark's close, near and far scenes
- The zip no longer has a `scvk.ini`. scvk still reads one when it is there

### Removed

- `UnlockRunningFPS`, which changed the same code as SC4CPUOptions and scd3d11

## [0.2.2] - 2026-10-17

### Added

- A `Use32BitDepth` setting in `scvk.ini` that brings back the 32-bit depth buffer of 0.2.0, off by default

### Changed

- The depth buffer is 16-bit, as on the game's DirectX renderer. Surfaces that sit very close together now band where DirectX bands too

### Removed

- The 0.2.1 change for the lines around ground lights, which turned other lines into patches of texture

### Fixed

- Thin lines around ground lights that sit exactly on their model after scrolling slowly, seen on an AMD RX 570

## [0.2.1] - 2026-10-11 [YANKED]

### Fixed

- Thin lines could appear around ground lights after scrolling slowly, seen on an AMD RX 570

## [0.2.0] - 2026-10-10

### Added

- scvk also takes the game's default DirectX slot, so installing it is copying two files and sc4-graphics-options is optional
- On a machine without Vulkan, the game keeps its own DirectX renderer
- A frame callback that lets other plugins draw over the game
- A benchmark mode in `scvk.ini` that compares scvk with the game's DirectX renderer, off by default

### Changed

- Faster drawing, most of all zoomed out, where scvk used to be slower than DirectX

### Fixed

- The game crashed at startup, or showed an empty region view, at 16-bit colour
- A paused city's frame rate was not unlocked when scd3d11 was installed too

## [0.1.2] - 2026-10-08

### Changed

- In fullscreen, the graphics driver can no longer take exclusive control of the screen, which should let PrintScreen capture the game on AMD graphics cards

## [0.1.1] - 2026-10-08

### Added

- A line in `scvk.log` once the first frame is on screen, confirming scvk is running

### Fixed

- Thin dark seams along the edges of street and lot tiles
- Two warnings `scvk.log` showed on every startup

## [0.1.0] - 2026-10-07

### Added

- A Vulkan renderer for SimCity 4, used when the game's driver is set to OpenGL
- Draws the region view, cities, menus and loading screens, windowed, full screen or borderless
- Lighting that matches the DirectX renderer, with cloud shadows, building shadows and night lights
- In-game photos
- A paused city is no longer held at 30 frames a second
- `MaxFPS` and `UnlockRunningFPS` settings in `scvk.ini` to raise the game's frame rate caps
- A `LogLevel` setting in `scvk.ini` for `scvk.log`, written beside the DLL

[Unreleased]: https://github.com/aspctt/scvk/compare/0.5.0...HEAD
[0.5.0]: https://github.com/aspctt/scvk/compare/0.4.0...0.5.0
[0.4.0]: https://github.com/aspctt/scvk/compare/0.3.0...0.4.0

	<a alt="Buy Me a Coffee" href="https://buymeacoffee.com/aspctt"><img alt="Buy Me a Coffee" height="40" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@intergrav/devins-badges@3/assets/compact/donate/buymeacoffee-singular_vector.svg"></a>
</p>

<p align="center" style="text-align: center;">
	<a alt="Available on GitHub" href="https://github.com/aspctt/scvk"><img alt="Available on GitHub" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@intergrav/devins-badges@3/assets/compact-minimal/available/github_vector.svg"></a>
	<a alt="Available on STEX" href="https://community.simtropolis.com/files/file/37697-scvk-dll/"><img alt="Available on STEX" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/aspctt/aspctt-badges@main/assets/compact-minimal/available/simtropolis_vector.svg"></a>
</p>

A native Vulkan renderer for SimCity 4.

SimCity 4 shipped in 2003 with a DirectX 7 renderer and an unfinished OpenGL
one. Both have aged badly against modern drivers. scvk replaces the renderer
with one built on Vulkan, loaded as a DLL plugin through the game's own GZCOM
plugin system.

This project is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Electronic
Arts Inc. or Maxis. Vulkan and the Vulkan logo are registered trademarks of the
Khronos Group Inc.

## Status

**Stable.** The whole game draws, from the region view to cities, menus and loading
screens. It has been played on NVIDIA and AMD graphics cards, on Windows and on Linux,
and Intel graphics are untested.

| Area | Status |
|---|---|
| Startup, video modes, swapchain | Working, windowed, fullscreen and borderless |
| Terrain, buildings, interface | Working |
| Textures, blending, depth | Working |
| Day and night lighting, cloud shadows | Working |
| Loading screens | Working |
| Fog | Working, though the game never turns it on |
| In-game photos | Working |
| ReShade | Working, effects under the interface with the city's depth |
| Live True3D shadows | Off by default, see [Live shadows](#live-shadows) |
| Performance | Faster than DirectX 7 in every [benchmark](#benchmark) scene, most of all zoomed out |

Known issues:

- An NVIDIA profile for SimCity 4 that differs from the global settings, such as
  Monitor Technology set to Fixed Refresh while G-SYNC is on, can blank the screen for
  a moment on Alt+Tab in borderless, like a resolution change. Resetting the profile
  to the global settings avoids it.

## How it works

SimCity 4 selects a renderer by GZCOM class ID and knows exactly three:
DirectX (`0xBADB6906`), OpenGL (`0xC4554841`), and Software (`0x7ACA35C6`).
There is no way to register a fourth. scvk therefore claims the **OpenGL class
ID** and registers at a higher version so the GZCOM prefers it over the game's
built-in driver. It claims the **DirectX class ID**, the game's default, as well,
one version lower, so the game picks scvk without any settings while a renderer
built for that slot, such as [scd3d11](https://github.com/caspervg/scd3d11), still
takes it.

> **scvk and [SCGL](https://github.com/nsgomez/scgl) cannot be installed at the
> same time.** Both claim the same class ID, and whichever registers the higher
> version silently wins. Install one or the other.

The interface the game expects, `cIGZGDriver`, is a fixed function API: roughly
OpenGL 1.2 with extensions, including a matrix stack, alpha test, fog, and
two-stage texture environment combiners. Vulkan has none of that. So scvk is
not a thin translation layer but a fixed function emulator, which is why the
design centres on a packed state key selecting a cached pipeline, with an
ubershader reproducing the combiner network in fragment code.

The game draws into a back buffer of scvk's own, the size of its video mode, and scvk
copies it into the window when the frame is shown. The back buffer survives from one
frame to the next, as DirectX's does, since the game only redraws what changed.

### Depth buffer

The game's DirectX renderer takes the first depth format the graphics card lists,
which is 16-bit on NVIDIA, and custom content is made for that. Lights laid exactly
on a model only line up with it after 16-bit rounding, so scvk uses a 16-bit depth
buffer too, and surfaces that sit very close together band as they do on DirectX.

The depth buffer has an 8-bit stencil as well, which the game never uses but
SC4RenderServices does, from 0.8.3 on, to draw terrain decals back over shadows once
per pixel. Not every card pairs 16-bit depth with a stencil, and on those scvk takes a
24-bit or 32-bit one and rounds every depth to 16 bits itself.

`-DepthBuffer:32` or `Use32BitDepth=true` in `scvk.ini` gives a 32-bit depth buffer,
as scvk had up to 0.2.0. The banding goes away, but those lights can leave thin lines
after scrolling. `-DepthBuffer:16` keeps the default for a launch whatever the ini says.
scd3d11's `-Depth16:off` and `-Depth16:on` do the same as `-DepthBuffer:32` and `16`.

### Window modes

scvk starts the game borderless: a window with no frame that covers the main monitor,
at the desktop's current size. The display keeps its mode, and other windows can be
switched to over the game. The city scrolls when the cursor reaches the screen's edge,
as in exclusive fullscreen.

In borderless and fullscreen the cursor stays on the main monitor while the game is in
front, and goes free again when another window is switched to.

Launch options pick another mode for that launch. `-w` or `-windowed` gives a window
and `-f` or `-fullscreen` exclusive fullscreen, both at the size in the game's
options, and `-r` sets a size of its own. `-b` or `-borderless` asks for borderless
outright and leaves out any `-r` size, while `-borderless:off` keeps the mode in the
game's options.

With sc4-graphics-options installed, its `WindowMode` decides instead, and its
`Borderless` gives the same window. `-b` still wins over its other modes. When the
game falls back to its own renderer, it keeps the mode from its options.

### Colour depth and resolution

scvk draws in 32-bit colour, but in a 16-bit mode the game makes its own textures
16-bit, and they band. Its options and the `-r` launch option can ask for 16 bits, so
scvk sets the game's colour depth to 32 at startup and saves it in the game's
preferences.

scvk also uses a `-r` size as given. Without `-CustomResolution:enabled`, the game
swaps a size it does not know for one of its own, so `-r1920x1080` became 1800x1440.
`-CustomResolution:disabled` keeps the game's size.

With sc4-graphics-options installed, its settings decide both instead. A fullscreen
size the display does not offer still drops the game to 16 bits at a smaller size,
with any renderer.

### Live shadows

SimCity 4 draws most shadows as flat pictures laid on the ground. scd3d11 added live
shadows, which draw True3D props and network pieces into a shadow map from the sun, so
their shadows follow slopes and fall across other buildings. scvk carries them over and
leaves them off by default, as scd3d11 does. While they are on, every scroll, zoom and
turn makes the game redraw the whole city instead of the strip that came into view.

`-NativeShadowMasks:network`, `props` or `all` turns them on for network pieces, props
or both. `-NativeShadowMasks:replace` adds the shadow registry, which takes over the
game's own shadows of buildings, trees and poles, and replaces the terrain's own
shading as well. It is experimental, and in a city of dense parks and raised roads it
laid blocks of shadow across the roads. `-LiveShadows:on` is the same as `replace`,
under the name scd3d11 uses now.

### ReShade

Installed for Vulkan, ReShade draws its effects over the whole frame, interface
included. With ReShade's full add-on support build, scvk registers as an add-on, as
scd3d11 does. The effects then draw once the city view is done and before the
interface goes over it, and effects that read depth get the city's own.
`-ReShade:off` leaves ReShade drawing over everything.

### Launch options

scvk takes scd3d11's launch options, so a launcher set up for one renderer works with
the other. An option that turns something on or off means on by itself, and after a
colon it takes `on`, `off`, `true`, `false`, `enabled`, `disabled`, `1` or `0`.

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `-d:Vulkan` | Picks scvk for this launch, whatever scd3d11 or `Driver=` in `SC4GraphicsOptions.ini` would choose |
| `-VSync:off` | Lets the frame rate go past the display's refresh rate |
| `-GPU:default` | Uses the first graphics card Vulkan lists, the way Windows picks, instead of preferring a dedicated one |
| `-GPU:<n>` | Uses the nth graphics card in `scvk.log`'s list, counted from 1 |
| `-FlipModel:off` | Presents a window or borderless game with one image fewer, as exclusive fullscreen does |
| `-ReShade:off` | Leaves ReShade drawing over the interface |
| `-ViewportCull:off` | Sends every draw of a scroll to the graphics card, instead of leaving out those outside the strip being redrawn |
| `-NativeShadowMasks:<mode>` | Turns on [live shadows](#live-shadows) |
| `-LiveShadows:on` or `-LiveShadows:off` | The same as `-NativeShadowMasks:replace` or `off` |
| `-MaxFPS:<n>` or `-MaxFPS:off` | Sets the [speed caps](#fps-limits-built-in) |
| `-DepthBuffer:32` or `-DepthBuffer:16` | Picks the [depth buffer](#depth-buffer), 16-bit by default |
| `-Depth16:off` or `-Depth16:on` | The same as `-DepthBuffer:32` or `16`, under scd3d11's name |
| `-LogLevel:<level>` | Sets how much goes into `scvk.log`, from `trace` to `off` |
| `-DoctorDialog:off` | Keeps setup problems in `scvk.log` only, the same as `DoctorDialog=false` in `scvk.ini` |
| `-FullscreenMode:Borderless` | The same as `-borderless` |

## Compatibility with other mods

- [SC4Fix](https://github.com/nsgomez/sc4fix): fully compatible.
- [sc4-graphics-options](https://github.com/0xC0000054/sc4-graphics-options): fully
  compatible, and the easiest way to choose between renderers. See
  [Installing](#installing).
- [scd3d11](https://github.com/caspervg/scd3d11): can be installed alongside, and
  keeps the DirectX slot. While it draws, scvk stays idle: no Vulkan, no patches and
  no changes to the video mode. See [Installing](#installing).

### FPS limits: built in

SimCity 4 caps its frame rate by simulation speed, at 30 for Turtle, 20 for
Rhino and 15 for Cheetah, by filling the rest of each frame with simulation.
A paused city is held at 30 the same way, though there is nothing to simulate.
That is the 30 a still camera settles at; the game skips the padding while the
camera moves.

scvk always lifts the paused 30. A paused city can then run at hundreds of
frames a second, where the game's animation clock rounded each frame up to 2 ms
and sped lot animations up, so scvk also lets it count short frames as they
are.

The speed caps go up to the display's refresh rate, so
[sc4-disable-fps-limits](https://github.com/caspervg/sc4-disable-fps-limits) is
not required, though it remains compatible, and caps it has already changed stay as
it set them. `-MaxFPS:<n>` sets the caps to a number of your own, and `-MaxFPS:off`
keeps the game's. `MaxFPS` in `scvk.ini` does the same, where 0 keeps the game's
caps, as it did in 0.2.

A running city still gets at least 15 ms of simulation every frame, which keeps it
near 60 frames a second whatever the cap. Raised caps take simulation time at Rhino
and Cheetah, so a heavy city can simulate more slowly, and `-MaxFPS:off` is the way
back.

This lives in scvk because frame pacing and presentation are one concern. Once
the swapchain exists, the present mode and this cap have to agree, and keeping
them in separate plugins means two settings files that can contradict one
another.

scvk is more cautious than it strictly needs to be here. It requires game
version 641, and it reads each byte before changing it: if a byte does not hold
the value it expects, it leaves the byte alone and says so in the log instead of
overwriting whatever is actually there, so running both plugins is safe.

[scd3d11](https://github.com/caspervg/scd3d11) and SC4CPUOptions limit each frame's
simulation time by changing the code next to scvk's, and both work alongside it.

### Drawing over the game from another plugin

scvk.dll exports two functions that let another plugin draw over every frame, such as
an overlay made with Dear ImGui. They work like scd3d11's frame callback, with Vulkan in
place of Direct3D 11:

```c
BOOL __stdcall SCVKRegisterFrameCallback(SCVKFrameCallback callback, void* userData);
BOOL __stdcall SCVKUnregisterFrameCallback(SCVKFrameCallback callback, void* userData);
```

The callback runs on the game's main thread once a frame, after the game has drawn
everything including its interface. It gets the instance, device, queue and loader, and a
command buffer already inside a render pass on scvk's back buffer, which is copied into
the window right after. It runs once more, with the device idle, before scvk destroys a
device, which it does for every video mode the game sets. [`src/SCVKFrameCallback.h`](src/SCVKFrameCallback.h) is the whole contract
and depends on nothing else, so a plugin copies it as it is. There is no import library:
find `scvk.dll` with `GetModuleHandleW` and look the functions up with `GetProcAddress`.

## Building

Requires Visual Studio 2022 or later with the desktop C++ workload. The Vulkan
headers are in `vendor/vulkan`, so the Vulkan SDK is only needed for the validation
layers.

```
msbuild scvk.sln /p:Configuration=Release /p:Platform=Win32
```

SimCity 4 is a 32-bit process, so **Win32 is the only supported platform**.
There is deliberately no x64 configuration.

Warnings are strict and treated as errors, so a build that warns does not
finish.

### Vulkan SDK

scvk loads `vulkan-1.dll` by name rather than linking `vulkan-1.lib`, so the
SDK is only needed at build time and users do not need it installed. Nothing
Vulkan-specific ships with the DLL.

The build looks for the SDK in this order: an explicit
`/p:VulkanSdkDir=<root>`, then a `VULKAN_SDK_32` environment variable, then a
local `1.3.296.0` install, then `VULKAN_SDK`, and without any of them it uses the
headers in `vendor/vulkan`.

> **For validation layers, use SDK 1.3.296.0.** SimCity 4 is a 32-bit process,
> so the layers must be 32-bit to load into it, and 1.3.296.0 is the last
> release that ships 32-bit components at all. Later SDKs are 64-bit only and
> their layers will silently not load. Only the layers care; the headers are
> architecture independent, so a newer SDK still builds fine, just without
> validation.

Debug builds enable the validation layers when they are present and route
their output into `scvk.log`, which is the only channel visible when running
inside the game. Release builds enable neither. The layers check every draw,
which makes a Debug build many times slower, so measure performance in Release.

### Shaders

GLSL lives in `shaders/`. It is compiled to SPIR-V and embedded into
`src/ShaderBinaries.h`, which is **committed**, so building scvk needs no
shader compiler and the DLL ships no external shader files.

Regenerate only after changing a shader, with PowerShell or Python:

```
pwsh shaders/compile.ps1
python3 shaders/compile.py
```

### Linux

`tools/build-mingw.sh` builds the same 32-bit DLL on Linux with MinGW-w64, without the
game-side shadow modules, which hook the game with MSVC-only assembly. GitHub runs it
in both configurations on every push (`.github/workflows/mingw.yml`).
`tests/wine/run.sh` builds a harness that loads the DLL the way the game does and
checks every draw path pixel by pixel under Wine, without the game. The harness also
builds with Visual Studio and runs on Windows.

## Diagnostics

`tools/run-sc4.ps1` deploys a build, runs the game for a set time and collects
the log. Options are listed at the top of the script.

Launch with `-LogLevel:trace`, or set `LogLevel=trace` in `scvk.ini`, to see
everything the game asks of the renderer in `scvk.log`, and `debug` for the statistics
below without that. At either level a few screenshots (`scvk-frame-N.bmp`,
`scvk-region-N.bmp`) are saved beside it during a session, and Scroll Lock in game
saves one on demand, along with the saved scene and its depth (`scvk-key-N-*`).

Every 300 frames the log also notes the frame rate, the slowest frame and how
its time split between the game and scvk's own work (drawing, copying geometry,
textures, and waiting for the graphics card), how many textures are loaded and
how many were created, deleted or uploaded since the last note, how much
geometry was copied, how many blocks of graphics memory the textures share, how
many memory allocations scvk holds against the graphics driver's limit, and how
strong the game asked the building shadows to be.

When the game stops drawing for five seconds, the log says where it was. A stall while
the game works on its own, such as a city loading, is one line, and a stall inside
scvk is a warning with its call stack. A crash leaves the faulting address, the
registers and the stack in the log as well.

To see a debug view, put an empty file with one of these names next to
`scvk.dll`, and delete it to go back to normal:

- `scvk-debug-passes`: colours each draw by how it blends
- `scvk-debug-texture-colour` or `scvk-debug-texture-alpha`: the texture alone
- `scvk-debug-vertex-colour` or `scvk-debug-vertex-alpha`: the lit vertex
  colour alone
- `scvk-skip-cloud-shadows`: leaves out the cloud shadows
- `scvk-force-fog`: draws the fog the city view would use if its fog were on, which
  fades the far distance to white
- `scvk-validate-sync`: in Debug builds, also checks the GPU work is correctly
  ordered (slow)
- `scvk-record-tile-draws`: Scroll Lock also saves every recent draw of the
  parts of the scene the game redrew, and of the moving things drawn over it
  (`scvk-key-N-draws.bin`), which `tools/draw-records.py` reads, and its log
  lists what kinds of draws made up each redrawn part (slow)
- `scvk-small-texture-pools`: makes room for only 64 textures at a time before
  scvk has to set aside more, so an ordinary session tests that it does
- `scvk-prefer-integrated-gpu`: runs on the processor's built-in graphics instead
  of the graphics card, to test another maker's driver on the same machine

## Benchmark

`tools/benchmark.ps1` compares scvk with the game's own DirectX 7 driver on a city
of your choice:

```
pwsh tools/benchmark.ps1 -Region "Blackfall" -City "Ostton" -Runs 2
```

Each run starts the game through Steam, which asks for a click, and the rest
happens by itself. scvk opens the region and the city, pauses it and times every
frame through eight camera scenes: a still view, scrolling at each zoom level, a
full turn and a run of zoom changes. It then writes `scvk-benchmark.csv` and
quits. The runs alternate between the two renderers, and
`tools/benchmark-report.py` turns them into average fps, 1% and 0.1% lows, frame
pacing and load times for each. Pacing covers the median and 99th percentile frame
time, stutters a minute and the average change from one frame to the next, since a few
long frames feel rough without moving the averages much.

With VSync on, the lighter scenes sit at the monitor's refresh rate. Add
`-GameArguments "-VSync:off"` to see how far past it scvk goes.

DirectX runs keep scvk loaded without its renderer, so both get the same frame
pacing fixes. Without them a paused city sits at 30 frames a second on DirectX,
and the comparison would measure that instead. A single run can also be started
by hand from the `[Benchmark]` section of `scvk.ini`.

## Installing

scvk needs Windows 10 or 11 or Linux through Wine or Proton, a graphics card with
Vulkan support and game version 641.

With [sc4pac](https://memo33.github.io/sc4pac/), install `aspct:scvk`. It uses the
`Plugins` folder in `Documents\SimCity 4` by default, so remove any copy from the
game's own `Plugins` folder first.

By hand, download the zip from the [releases page](https://github.com/aspctt/scvk/releases)
and copy `scvk.dll` into a `Plugins` folder, either the one in your SimCity 4
installation or the one in `Documents\SimCity 4`, but not both.

With `-UserDir`, the `Plugins` folder in that folder takes the place of the one in
`Documents\SimCity 4`, and a path with spaces needs quotes, as in
`-UserDir:"D:\My Games\SimCity 4\"`. Without them the game cuts the path at the first
space and looks in the wrong folder, so a `scvk.dll` there never loads.

That is all: the game picks scvk by default. On a machine without Vulkan, the game
keeps its own DirectX renderer.

With [sc4-graphics-options](https://github.com/0xC0000054/sc4-graphics-options),
both `Driver=DirectX` and `Driver=OpenGL` select scvk. With scd3d11 installed as
well, `DirectX` selects scd3d11 and `OpenGL` selects scvk. scvk draws in 32-bit
whatever `ColorDepth` says. Set it to 32 for windowed play: at 16, the game switches
to fullscreen whenever the desktop runs at a different depth, with any renderer.

With `Driver=DirectX` and no scd3d11, `SC4GraphicsOptions.log` says "Failed to set
the game's driver to DirectX." on every start. Nothing failed. scvk is drawing, but
it reports the OpenGL ID from either slot, which is what sc4-graphics-options
checks. `Driver=OpenGL` keeps that log quiet.

```ini
[GraphicsOptions]
Driver=OpenGL
ColorDepth=32
```

> **`Driver=OpenGL` does not select SC4's own unfinished OpenGL renderer.**
>
> This trips people up, because that renderer is famously broken and cannot
> start a game. But the game resolves a renderer by class ID, and the GZCOM
> hands out the highest-version registrant for a given class. scvk registers
> the OpenGL class ID at version 1000000 against the built-in driver's 0, so
> asking for OpenGL gets you scvk and the built-in driver never runs. SCGL
> works the same way, which is why graphics-options accepts `Driver=SCGL` as a
> literal alias for the same entry.
>
> The game starts a driver for every slot and keeps them all until it exits, so
> the log shows a second scvk driver that starts, never draws and shuts down at
> exit. That is the slot the game is not using.

A `scvk.log` file is written next to the DLL, falling back to the temp
directory if the Plugins folder is not writable. It opens with the game's command line
and the `scvk.ini` scvk read, or that there is none. `-LogLevel:<level>` sets how much
goes into it, from `trace` to `off`, and is `info` by default. When the game starts,
scvk looks over your setup and writes what it finds there: another driver drawing, a
plugin loaded twice or unable to load, an old SC4RenderServices, no 4GB patch,
compatibility mode and mistyped launch options or settings. Serious problems also show
in a dialog when the region view opens, and `DoctorDialog=false` in `scvk.ini` or
`-DoctorDialog:off` keeps them in the log. Paths in the log and the dialog show your
Windows account as `%USERPROFILE%` or `%USERNAME%`, so a log can be posted as it is.

`scvk.ini` is optional. scvk reads it from beside the DLL when it is there, for
`MaxFPS`, `Use32BitDepth`, `LogLevel`, `DoctorDialog` and the benchmark, and the
[`scvk.ini`](scvk.ini) in the zip explains each. sc4pac installs that file as
`scvk_sc4pacnew.ini`, so rename it to use it. A `scvk.ini` from 0.2 keeps working.

To turn scvk off without removing it, put a `scvk.ini` next to the DLL with
`Enabled=false` under `[Admin]`. The game itself reads that setting, so scvk is never
loaded at all. That is also the way back to the game's DirectX renderer.

<h1 id="scvk">scvk</h1>
<p>A native Vulkan renderer for SimCity 4.</p>
<p>SimCity 4 shipped in 2003 with a DirectX 7 renderer and an unfinished OpenGL
one. scvk replaces the renderer with one built on Vulkan, loaded as a DLL plugin
through the game's own plugin system.</p>
<p>This project is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Electronic
Arts Inc. or Maxis. Vulkan and the Vulkan logo are registered trademarks of the
Khronos Group Inc.</p>

<h2 id="status">Status</h2>
<p><strong>Stable.</strong> The region view, cities, menus and loading
screens all draw, windowed, full screen or borderless, with lighting that matches
the DirectX renderer, and it is faster than DirectX, most of all zoomed out.
ReShade's effects draw under the interface, and scd3d11's live shadows can be
turned on. Players have run it on NVIDIA and AMD graphics cards, on Windows and on
Linux, and Intel graphics are untested.</p>

<h2 id="system-requirements">System Requirements</h2>
<ul>
<li>SimCity 4 Deluxe, game version 641. Older versions are untested.</li>
<li>Windows 10 or 11, or Linux through Wine or Proton.</li>
<li>A graphics card and driver with Vulkan support.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="installation">Installation</h2>
<ol type="1">
<li>Close SimCity 4.</li>
<li>Copy <code>scvk.dll</code> into a Plugins folder, either the one in the
SimCity 4 installation directory or the one in Documents\SimCity 4, but not
both.</li>
<li>Start the game. A <code>scvk.log</code> file appears beside
<code>scvk.dll</code>.</li>
</ol>
<p>With <code>-UserDir</code>, the Plugins folder in that folder takes the place of
the one in Documents\SimCity 4, and a path with spaces needs quotes, as in
<code>-UserDir:"D:\My Games\SimCity 4\"</code>. Without them the game cuts the path
at the first space and looks in the wrong folder, so a <code>scvk.dll</code> there
never loads.</p>
<p>That is all: the game picks scvk by default. On a machine without Vulkan, the
game keeps its own DirectX renderer.</p>
<p>With <a href="https://github.com/0xC0000054/sc4-graphics-options">sc4-graphics-options</a>,
both <code>Driver=DirectX</code> and <code>Driver=OpenGL</code> select scvk.
<code>Driver=OpenGL</code> does not start the game's own unfinished OpenGL
renderer, since scvk registers under that ID with a higher version. scvk draws in
32-bit whatever <code>ColorDepth</code> says. Set it to 32 for windowed play: at
16, the game switches to fullscreen whenever the desktop runs at a different
depth.</p>
<p>With <code>Driver=DirectX</code>, <code>SC4GraphicsOptions.log</code> says
"Failed to set the game's driver to DirectX." on every start. Nothing failed.
scvk is drawing, but it reports the OpenGL ID from either slot.
<code>Driver=OpenGL</code> keeps that log quiet.</p>
<p>To go back to DirectX, remove <code>scvk.dll</code>, or see <code>Enabled</code>
below.</p>

<h2 id="settings">Settings</h2>
<p>scvk needs no settings. Launch options change a few things for one launch:</p>
<ul>
<li>scvk starts the game borderless, covering the main monitor. The city scrolls
at the screen's edges, and the cursor stays on that monitor while the game is in
front. <code>-w</code>
gives a window and <code>-f</code> exclusive fullscreen, at the size in the game's
options, and <code>-r</code> sets a size of its own. <code>-borderless:off</code>
keeps the mode in the game's options. With sc4-graphics-options installed, its
<code>WindowMode</code> decides instead.</li>
<li><code>-NativeShadowMasks:all</code> turns on live shadows for True3D props and
network pieces. They are off by default, since while they are on every scroll,
zoom and turn makes the game redraw the whole city.
<code>-NativeShadowMasks:replace</code> adds the experimental shadow registry and
terrain shadows, and <code>-LiveShadows:on</code>, scd3d11's name for it, does the
same.</li>
<li><code>-d:Vulkan</code> picks scvk for this launch, whatever scd3d11 or
<code>Driver=</code> in <code>SC4GraphicsOptions.ini</code> would choose.</li>
<li><code>-MaxFPS:&lt;n&gt;</code> sets the game's frame rate caps, which are 30 at
Turtle speed, 20 at Rhino and 15 at Cheetah. scvk raises them to the display's
refresh rate by default, and <code>-MaxFPS:off</code> keeps the game's. A paused
city is never held at 30 whatever this says.</li>
<li><code>-DepthBuffer:32</code> gives the depth buffer 32 bits instead of the 16 the
DirectX renderer uses. Surfaces that sit very close together stop banding, but lights
laid exactly on a model can leave thin lines after scrolling.
<code>-DepthBuffer:16</code> keeps the default. scd3d11's <code>-Depth16:off</code>
and <code>-Depth16:on</code> do the same.</li>
<li><code>-VSync:off</code>, <code>-GPU:default</code>, <code>-FlipModel:off</code>,
<code>-ViewportCull:off</code> and <code>-ReShade:off</code> work as they do in
scd3d11.</li>
<li><code>-GPU:&lt;n&gt;</code> uses the nth graphics card in the list in
<code>scvk.log</code>, counted from 1.</li>
<li><code>-DoctorDialog:off</code> keeps setup problems in <code>scvk.log</code>
instead of showing them in a dialog when the region view opens.
<code>DoctorDialog=false</code> under <code>[scvk]</code> does the same.</li>
<li><code>-LogLevel:&lt;level&gt;</code> sets how much goes into
<code>scvk.log</code>, from <code>trace</code> to <code>off</code>.
<code>info</code> by default.</li>
</ul>
<p>Options that turn something on or off mean on by themselves, and after a colon
they take <code>on</code>, <code>off</code>, <code>true</code>, <code>false</code>,
<code>enabled</code>, <code>disabled</code>, <code>1</code> or <code>0</code>, as in
scd3d11.</p>
<p>The <code>scvk.ini</code> in the zip is optional. Copy it beside
<code>scvk.dll</code> if you want to change a setting, and scvk reads it when it is
there. A <code>scvk.ini</code> from 0.2 keeps working, but its
<code>MaxFPS=0</code> keeps the game's frame rate caps; delete that line for the
display's refresh rate.</p>
<p><code>MaxFPS</code> under <code>[scvk]</code> does what <code>-MaxFPS</code>
does, where 0 keeps the game's caps.</p>
<p><code>Use32BitDepth=true</code> under <code>[scvk]</code> does what
<code>-DepthBuffer:32</code> does.</p>
<p><code>LogLevel</code> under <code>[scvk]</code> does what
<code>-LogLevel</code> does.</p>
<p><code>Enabled=false</code> under <code>[Admin]</code> stops the game loading
scvk at all, which brings back the DirectX renderer. If
<code>SC4GraphicsOptions.ini</code> says <code>Driver=OpenGL</code>, set it to
<code>DirectX</code> as well, or the game falls back to its own OpenGL renderer,
which does not work.</p>
<p>The frame rate changes only apply to game version 641, and scvk checks the
game's code holds what it expects before changing anything.</p>

<h2 id="compatibility">Compatibility</h2>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/nsgomez/scgl">SCGL</a> cannot be installed at the
same time. Both register as the OpenGL renderer, so install one or the
other.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/nsgomez/sc4fix">SC4Fix</a> is fully compatible.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/0xC0000054/sc4-graphics-options">sc4-graphics-options</a>
is fully compatible, though no longer needed to choose scvk.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/caspervg/scd3d11">scd3d11</a> can be installed
alongside. It keeps the DirectX slot, so <code>Driver=DirectX</code> selects
scd3d11 and <code>Driver=OpenGL</code> selects scvk. While scd3d11 draws, scvk
stays idle and changes nothing in the game.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/caspervg/sc4-disable-fps-limits">sc4-disable-fps-limits</a>
works alongside scvk, and the caps it sets stay.</li>
<li><a href="https://reshade.me">ReShade</a> 6, installed for Vulkan with full
add-on support, draws its effects under the interface, with the city's depth for
effects that read it. Without full add-on support, its effects cover the interface
too.</li>
<li>DirectX wrappers such as dgVoodoo 2 only affect the DirectX renderer. scvk
does not need one, and they can stay installed.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="troubleshooting">Troubleshooting</h2>
<p><code>scvk.log</code> is written beside <code>scvk.dll</code>, or in the
Windows temp folder if the Plugins folder cannot be written to. It names the
graphics card scvk chose and its driver, lists the plugins that loaded and notes
anything that went wrong. Paths in it show your Windows account as
<code>%USERPROFILE%</code> or <code>%USERNAME%</code>, so it can be posted as it
is.</p>
<p>scvk also looks over your setup when the game starts, for things like another
driver drawing, a plugin loaded twice, a SC4RenderServices older than 0.8.3, no 4GB
patch or a mistyped launch option. Serious problems show in a dialog when the region
view opens.</p>
<p>If there is no log at all, the game did not load scvk. Check that
<code>scvk.dll</code> is directly in a Plugins folder, not in a subfolder, and
that <code>Enabled</code> is not set to false in <code>scvk.ini</code>.</p>
<p>Please report problems at
<a href="https://github.com/aspctt/scvk/issues">https://github.com/aspctt/scvk/issues</a>,
with your <code>scvk.log</code>, your graphics card and its driver version.</p>

`scvk.ini`:

```ini
; scvk settings
; This file is optional, and scvk runs fine without it. If you want it, keep it
; next to scvk.dll. Lines starting with a semicolon are comments.

[Admin]
; Set this to false to turn scvk off without removing it. The game reads this
; itself and goes back to its DirectX renderer.
Enabled=true

[scvk]
; The frame rate limit for a running city. The game's own limits are 30 on
; Turtle, 20 on Rhino and 15 on Cheetah, and scvk raises all three to your
; monitor's refresh rate, so most people can leave this alone. To pick your own
; limit, remove the semicolon and set a number up to 255. 0 keeps the game's
; limits. -MaxFPS:<n> or -MaxFPS:off in your launch options does the same and
; wins over this line.
;
; A running city stays near 60 frames a second whatever you set here, since the
; game gives every frame at least 15 ms of simulation. A higher limit can slow
; down a heavy city on Rhino and Cheetah. With sc4-disable-fps-limits installed
; this does nothing, because that plugin's limits stay.
;MaxFPS=0

; Set this to true for a 32-bit depth buffer instead of the 16-bit one DirectX
; uses. Surfaces sitting very close together stop banding, but lights laid
; exactly on a model can leave thin lines after scrolling, since custom content
; is made for 16 bits. -DepthBuffer:32 or -DepthBuffer:16 in your launch options
; does the same and wins over this line.
Use32BitDepth=false

; How much scvk writes to scvk.log, next to scvk.dll. From least to most: off,
; critical, error, warn, info, debug, trace.
;
; info is the default and shows your graphics card, the video mode and anything
; that went wrong. debug adds statistics, drawing diagnostics and a few
; screenshots, and trace also lists every call the game makes into scvk while
; it starts.
LogLevel=info

; scvk looks over your setup when the game starts and writes what it finds to
; scvk.log. Serious problems also show in a dialog when the region view opens.
; Set this to false to keep them in the log only. -DoctorDialog:off in your
; launch options does the same and wins over this line.
DoctorDialog=true

[Benchmark]
; Runs a benchmark instead of a normal game. scvk opens the region and city
; below, pauses the city, times every frame through the same camera moves,
; writes scvk-benchmark.csv next to scvk.dll and quits. tools/benchmark.ps1 in
; scvk's source sets this up for you and compares scvk with DirectX.
Enabled=false

; What to measure: scvk, or DirectX for the game's own driver. DirectX also
; needs Driver=DirectX in SC4GraphicsOptions.ini.
Renderer=scvk

; The region to open, as the region view names it. Leave it empty for the one
; the game opens with.
Region=

; The city to open, as the region view names it, or its save file, such as
; City - Springfield.sc4.
City=

; How many seconds each camera move is timed, from 1 to 600.
SceneSeconds=20

; Quits the game once the results are written.
QuitWhenDone=true

```

    <RootNamespace>scvk</RootNamespace>
    <WindowsTargetPlatformVersion>10.0</WindowsTargetPlatformVersion>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <Import Project="$(VCTargetsPath)\Microsoft.Cpp.Default.props" />
  <!--
    SimCity 4 is a 32-bit process, so the driver has to be a 32-bit DLL. There
    is deliberately no x64 configuration; adding one would only produce a
    binary the game cannot load.
  -->
  <PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)|$(Platform)'=='Debug|Win32'" Label="Configuration">
    <ConfigurationType>DynamicLibrary</ConfigurationType>
    <UseDebugLibraries>true</UseDebugLibraries>
    <PlatformToolset>$(DefaultPlatformToolset)</PlatformToolset>
    <CharacterSet>MultiByte</CharacterSet>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)|$(Platform)'=='Release|Win32'" Label="Configuration">
    <ConfigurationType>DynamicLibrary</ConfigurationType>
    <UseDebugLibraries>false</UseDebugLibraries>
    <WholeProgramOptimization>true</WholeProgramOptimization>
    <PlatformToolset>$(DefaultPlatformToolset)</PlatformToolset>
    <CharacterSet>MultiByte</CharacterSet>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <Import Project="$(VCTargetsPath)\Microsoft.Cpp.props" />
  <ImportGroup Label="PropertySheets">
    <Import Project="$(UserRootDir)\Microsoft.Cpp.$(Platform).user.props" Condition="exists('$(UserRootDir)\Microsoft.Cpp.$(Platform).user.props')" Label="LocalAppDataPlatform" />
  </ImportGroup>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetName>scvk</TargetName>
    <OutDir>$(SolutionDir)$(Configuration)\</OutDir>
    <IntDir>$(SolutionDir)obj\$(Configuration)\</IntDir>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <!--
    Vulkan SDK location.

    SimCity 4 is a 32-bit process, so the validation layers have to be 32-bit
    to load into it. SDK 1.3.296.0 is the last release that ships 32-bit
    components at all; every later SDK is 64-bit only. Since the machine-wide
    VULKAN_SDK variable will normally point at a newer, 64-bit-only install,
    this deliberately prefers the older one.

    Only the layers actually require the old SDK. The headers are architecture
    independent and scvk loads vulkan-1.dll by name rather than linking against
    vulkan-1.lib, so nothing else here is version sensitive.

    Override order: an explicit /p:VulkanSdkDir=..., then a VULKAN_SDK_32
    environment variable, then the known 1.3.296.0 install, then whatever
    VULKAN_SDK points at, then the Vulkan 1.3.296 headers in vendor\vulkan, so
    a machine with no SDK at all still builds. Only the validation layers of a
    Debug build need a real SDK.
  -->
  <PropertyGroup Label="VulkanSdk">
    <VulkanSdkDir Condition="'$(VulkanSdkDir)' == '' And '$(VULKAN_SDK_32)' != ''">$(VULKAN_SDK_32)</VulkanSdkDir>
    <VulkanSdkDir Condition="'$(VulkanSdkDir)' == '' And Exists('S:\VulkanSDK\1.3.296.0\Include\vulkan\vulkan.h')">S:\VulkanSDK\1.3.296.0</VulkanSdkDir>
    <VulkanSdkDir Condition="'$(VulkanSdkDir)' == '' And '$(VULKAN_SDK)' != '' And Exists('$(VULKAN_SDK)\Include\vulkan\vulkan.h')">$(VULKAN_SDK)</VulkanSdkDir>
    <VulkanSdkDir Condition="'$(VulkanSdkDir)' == ''">$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)vendor\vulkan</VulkanSdkDir>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <!--
    Warnings.

    The strictest checking MSVC offers short of /Wall, whose extra noise is about
    padding, inlining and Spectre rather than types: level 4, conformance mode,
    warnings as errors, and the off-by-default conversion and override warnings
    on top. Headers included with angle brackets (Windows, Vulkan, the GZCOM SDK)
    are external and stay quiet, since they are not ours to fix.

    C4242, C4254, C4365, C4826 and C5219: narrowing and sign-changing conversions.
    C4263, C4264, C4265, C4266: virtual functions that fail to override or hide.
    C4062: an enumerator missing from a switch with no default.
    C4287, C4296: comparisons that are always true or always false.
    C4388: signed and unsigned comparisons.
  -->
  <PropertyGroup Label="Warnings">
    <ScvkExtraWarnings>/w44242 /w44254 /w44365 /w44826 /w45219 /w44263 /w44264 /w44265 /w44266 /w44062 /w44287 /w44296 /w44388</ScvkExtraWarnings>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <Target Name="ScvkCheckVulkanSdk" BeforeTargets="ClCompile">
    <Error Condition="!Exists('$(VulkanSdkDir)\Include\vulkan\vulkan.h')"
           Text="Vulkan headers not found in '$(VulkanSdkDir)'. vendor\vulkan\Include should hold them; set VULKAN_SDK_32 or pass /p:VulkanSdkDir=&lt;sdk root&gt; to use an SDK instead." />
    <Message Importance="high" Text="scvk: using the Vulkan headers at $(VulkanSdkDir)" />
  </Target>
  <!--
    C runtime.

    Linked statically, so players need no Visual C++ Redistributable, and in
    particular not one at least as new as the toolset that built the DLL. Its own
    heap is no change in practice: the game links its own static VC++ 2003 runtime,
    so nothing scvk allocates was ever freed by the game, or the other way round.
    Objects cross only through reference counted interfaces, which free themselves.
  -->
  <ItemDefinitionGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)|$(Platform)'=='Debug|Win32'">
    <ClCompile>
      <RuntimeLibrary>MultiThreadedDebug</RuntimeLibrary>
      <WarningLevel>Level4</WarningLevel>
      <TreatWarningAsError>true</TreatWarningAsError>
      <ConformanceMode>true</ConformanceMode>
      <TreatAngleIncludeAsExternal>true</TreatAngleIncludeAsExternal>
      <ExternalWarningLevel>TurnOffAllWarnings</ExternalWarningLevel>
      <AdditionalOptions>$(ScvkExtraWarnings) %(AdditionalOptions)</AdditionalOptions>
      <SDLCheck>true</SDLCheck>
      <PreprocessorDefinitions>WIN32;_DEBUG;_WINDOWS;_USRDLL;WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN;NOMINMAX;_CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS;%(PreprocessorDefinitions)</PreprocessorDefinitions>
      <AdditionalIncludeDirectories>$(ProjectDir)vendor\include;$(ProjectDir)vendor\reshade\include;$(ProjectDir)include;$(ProjectDir)src;$(VulkanSdkDir)\Include;%(AdditionalIncludeDirectories)</AdditionalIncludeDirectories>
      <LanguageStandard>stdcpp20</LanguageStandard>
      <MultiProcessorCompilation>true</MultiProcessorCompilation>
      <Optimization>Disabled</Optimization>
    </ClCompile>
    <Link>
      <SubSystem>Windows</SubSystem>
      <GenerateDebugInformation>true</GenerateDebugInformation>
      <AdditionalDependencies>version.lib;%(AdditionalDependencies)</AdditionalDependencies>
    </Link>
  </ItemDefinitionGroup>
  <ItemDefinitionGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)|$(Platform)'=='Release|Win32'">
    <ClCompile>
      <RuntimeLibrary>MultiThreaded</RuntimeLibrary>
      <WarningLevel>Level4</WarningLevel>
      <TreatWarningAsError>true</TreatWarningAsError>
      <ConformanceMode>true</ConformanceMode>
      <TreatAngleIncludeAsExternal>true</TreatAngleIncludeAsExternal>
      <ExternalWarningLevel>TurnOffAllWarnings</ExternalWarningLevel>
      <AdditionalOptions>$(ScvkExtraWarnings) %(AdditionalOptions)</AdditionalOptions>
      <FunctionLevelLinking>true</FunctionLevelLinking>
      <IntrinsicFunctions>true</IntrinsicFunctions>
      <SDLCheck>true</SDLCheck>
      <PreprocessorDefinitions>WIN32;NDEBUG;_WINDOWS;_USRDLL;WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN;NOMINMAX;_CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS;%(PreprocessorDefinitions)</PreprocessorDefinitions>
      <AdditionalIncludeDirectories>$(ProjectDir)vendor\include;$(ProjectDir)vendor\reshade\include;$(ProjectDir)include;$(ProjectDir)src;$(VulkanSdkDir)\Include;%(AdditionalIncludeDirectories)</AdditionalIncludeDirectories>
      <LanguageStandard>stdcpp20</LanguageStandard>

`shaders/compile.ps1`:

```ps1
# Compiles the GLSL sources to SPIR-V and regenerates src/ShaderBinaries.h.
#
# The generated header is committed, so building scvk needs no shader compiler. Run this
# only when a shader changes.
#
#   pwsh shaders/compile.ps1
#
# glslc comes with the Vulkan SDK. Set VULKAN_SDK_32 or VULKAN_SDK, or pass -Glslc with an
# explicit path.

param(
	[string]$Glslc = $null
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

#// Constants

$shaderDirectory = $PSScriptRoot
$outputFile      = Join-Path (Split-Path $shaderDirectory -Parent) "src\ShaderBinaries.h"

$header = @"
/*
 * scvk - a native Vulkan renderer for SimCity 4
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 aspctt
 *
 * This library is free software; you can redistribute it and/or
 * modify it under the terms of the GNU Lesser General Public
 * License as published by the Free Software Foundation, under
 * version 2.1 of the License, or (at your option) any later version.
 *
 * This library is distributed in the hope that it will be useful,
 * but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
 * MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.  See the GNU
 * Lesser General Public License for more details.
 *
 * You should have received a copy of the GNU Lesser General Public
 * License along with this library; if not, see <https://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.
 */

/*
 * GENERATED FILE. Do not edit.
 *
 * Produced from the GLSL in shaders/ by shaders/compile.ps1 or shaders/compile.py. It is
 * committed so that building scvk requires no shader compiler; regenerate it only when
 * a shader changes.
 */

#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>

namespace scvk
{
"@

# The vertex stage is built once per attribute combination. A shader may not declare an
# input the pipeline does not supply, and the game's vertex formats disagree about which
# of colour and texture coordinate are present. The fragment stage is built twice, the
# second time rounding the depth for a depth buffer with more than 16 bits.
#
# The names match the order the backend indexes them: the colour flag times three, plus
# the number of texture coordinate sets. shaders/compile.py builds the same list.
$stages = @(
	@{ file = "geometry.vert";    name = "GEOMETRY_VERTEX_SPIRV_NONE";            defines = @("SCVK_HAS_COLOUR=0", "SCVK_TEXTURE_COORDINATE_SETS=0") },
	@{ file = "geometry.vert";    name = "GEOMETRY_VERTEX_SPIRV_TEXTURE";         defines = @("SCVK_HAS_COLOUR=0", "SCVK_TEXTURE_COORDINATE_SETS=1") },
	@{ file = "geometry.vert";    name = "GEOMETRY_VERTEX_SPIRV_TEXTURE2";        defines = @("SCVK_HAS_COLOUR=0", "SCVK_TEXTURE_COORDINATE_SETS=2") },
	@{ file = "geometry.vert";    name = "GEOMETRY_VERTEX_SPIRV_COLOUR";          defines = @("SCVK_HAS_COLOUR=1", "SCVK_TEXTURE_COORDINATE_SETS=0") },
	@{ file = "geometry.vert";    name = "GEOMETRY_VERTEX_SPIRV_COLOUR_TEXTURE";  defines = @("SCVK_HAS_COLOUR=1", "SCVK_TEXTURE_COORDINATE_SETS=1") },
	@{ file = "geometry.vert";    name = "GEOMETRY_VERTEX_SPIRV_COLOUR_TEXTURE2"; defines = @("SCVK_HAS_COLOUR=1", "SCVK_TEXTURE_COORDINATE_SETS=2") },
	@{ file = "geometry.frag";    name = "GEOMETRY_FRAGMENT_SPIRV";               defines = @("SCVK_QUANTISE_DEPTH=0") },
	@{ file = "geometry.frag";    name = "GEOMETRY_FRAGMENT_SPIRV_QUANTISED";     defines = @("SCVK_QUANTISE_DEPTH=1") },
	@{ file = "shadow.vert";      name = "SHADOW_VERTEX_SPIRV";                   defines = @() },
	@{ file = "shadow.frag";      name = "SHADOW_FRAGMENT_SPIRV";                 defines = @() },
	@{ file = "fullscreen.vert";  name = "FULLSCREEN_VERTEX_SPIRV";               defines = @() },
	@{ file = "composite.frag";   name = "COMPOSITE_FRAGMENT_SPIRV";              defines = @() },
	@{ file = "scene_depth.frag"; name = "SCENE_DEPTH_FRAGMENT_SPIRV";            defines = @() }
)

# SPIR-V words per line of the generated arrays.
$wordsPerLine = 8

#// Private Functions

# Finds glslc in the SDKs this machine is known to have, when no path was given.
function Find-Glslc {
	foreach ($root in @($env:VULKAN_SDK_32, $env:VULKAN_SDK, "S:\VulkanSDK\1.3.296.0")) {
		if ($root -and (Test-Path "$root\Bin\glslc.exe")) {
			return "$root\Bin\glslc.exe"
		}
	}

	return $null
}

# Compiles one stage and returns its SPIR-V as a C++ array definition.
function Convert-Stage {
	param([hashtable]$Stage)

	# Compile it to a temporary file
	$source    = Join-Path $shaderDirectory $Stage.file
	$spirvFile = [System.IO.Path]::GetTempFileName() + ".spv"

	$compilerArguments = @("-O", "--target-env=vulkan1.0")
	foreach ($define in $Stage.defines) { $compilerArguments += "-D$define" }
	$compilerArguments += @($source, "-o", $spirvFile)

	& $Glslc @compilerArguments | Out-Host
	if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "glslc failed on $($Stage.name)" }

	$bytes = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($spirvFile)
	Remove-Item $spirvFile -Force

	if ($bytes.Length % 4 -ne 0) { throw "$($Stage.file): SPIR-V length is not a multiple of 4" }

	# Write it out as words, a line at a time
	$words = New-Object "System.Collections.Generic.List[string]"
	for ($i = 0; $i -lt $bytes.Length; $i += 4) {
		$word = [System.BitConverter]::ToUInt32($bytes, $i)
		$words.Add(("0x{0:x8}u" -f $word))
	}

	$definition = "`tinline constexpr uint32_t $($Stage.name)[] = {`n"
	for ($i = 0; $i -lt $words.Count; $i += $wordsPerLine) {
		$slice = $words[$i..([Math]::Min($i + $wordsPerLine - 1, $words.Count - 1))]
		$definition += "`t`t" + ($slice -join ", ") + ",`n"
	}
	$definition += "`t};`n`n"

	Write-Host ("{0,-40} {1,6} bytes, {2} words" -f $Stage.name, $bytes.Length, $words.Count)
	return $definition
}

#// Entry Point

if (-not $Glslc) {
	$Glslc = Find-Glslc
}

if (-not $Glslc -or -not (Test-Path $Glslc)) {
	throw "glslc not found. Pass -Glslc <path>, or set VULKAN_SDK."
}

$body = ""
foreach ($stage in $stages) {
	$body += Convert-Stage -Stage $stage
}

$footer = "}`n"

[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($outputFile, $header + "`n" + $body + $footer)
Write-Host "wrote $outputFile"

```

`shaders/compile.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Compiles the GLSL sources to SPIR-V and regenerates src/ShaderBinaries.h.
#
# The same job as compile.ps1, for machines with Python rather than PowerShell. Either
# glslc (Vulkan SDK) or glslangValidator does the compiling; spirv-opt, when present,
# optimises the result as glslc -O would.
#
#   python3 shaders/compile.py

import os
import shutil
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

SHADER_DIRECTORY = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
OUTPUT_FILE      = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(SHADER_DIRECTORY), "src", "ShaderBinaries.h")
WORDS_PER_LINE   = 8

HEADER = """/*
 * scvk - a native Vulkan renderer for SimCity 4
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 aspctt
 *
 * This library is free software; you can redistribute it and/or
 * modify it under the terms of the GNU Lesser General Public
 * License as published by the Free Software Foundation, under
 * version 2.1 of the License, or (at your option) any later version.
 *
 * This library is distributed in the hope that it will be useful,
 * but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
 * MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.  See the GNU
 * Lesser General Public License for more details.
 *
 * You should have received a copy of the GNU Lesser General Public
 * License along with this library; if not, see <https://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.
 */

/*
 * GENERATED FILE. Do not edit.
 *
 * Produced from the GLSL in shaders/ by shaders/compile.ps1 or shaders/compile.py. It is
 * committed so that building scvk requires no shader compiler; regenerate it only when
 * a shader changes.
 */

#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>

namespace scvk
{
"""

# The vertex stage is built once per attribute combination. The names match the order
# the backend indexes them: the colour flag times three, plus the number of texture
# coordinate sets. The fragment stage is built twice, the second time rounding the depth
# for a depth buffer with more than 16 bits. shaders/compile.ps1 builds the same list.
STAGES = [
    ("geometry.vert",    "GEOMETRY_VERTEX_SPIRV_NONE",            ["SCVK_HAS_COLOUR=0", "SCVK_TEXTURE_COORDINATE_SETS=0"]),
    ("geometry.vert",    "GEOMETRY_VERTEX_SPIRV_TEXTURE",         ["SCVK_HAS_COLOUR=0", "SCVK_TEXTURE_COORDINATE_SETS=1"]),
    ("geometry.vert",    "GEOMETRY_VERTEX_SPIRV_TEXTURE2",        ["SCVK_HAS_COLOUR=0", "SCVK_TEXTURE_COORDINATE_SETS=2"]),
    ("geometry.vert",    "GEOMETRY_VERTEX_SPIRV_COLOUR",          ["SCVK_HAS_COLOUR=1", "SCVK_TEXTURE_COORDINATE_SETS=0"]),
    ("geometry.vert",    "GEOMETRY_VERTEX_SPIRV_COLOUR_TEXTURE",  ["SCVK_HAS_COLOUR=1", "SCVK_TEXTURE_COORDINATE_SETS=1"]),
    ("geometry.vert",    "GEOMETRY_VERTEX_SPIRV_COLOUR_TEXTURE2", ["SCVK_HAS_COLOUR=1", "SCVK_TEXTURE_COORDINATE_SETS=2"]),
    ("geometry.frag",    "GEOMETRY_FRAGMENT_SPIRV",               ["SCVK_QUANTISE_DEPTH=0"]),
    ("geometry.frag",    "GEOMETRY_FRAGMENT_SPIRV_QUANTISED",     ["SCVK_QUANTISE_DEPTH=1"]),
    ("shadow.vert",      "SHADOW_VERTEX_SPIRV",                   []),
    ("shadow.frag",      "SHADOW_FRAGMENT_SPIRV",                 []),
    ("fullscreen.vert",  "FULLSCREEN_VERTEX_SPIRV",               []),
    ("composite.frag",   "COMPOSITE_FRAGMENT_SPIRV",              []),
    ("scene_depth.frag", "SCENE_DEPTH_FRAGMENT_SPIRV",            []),
]


def compile_stage(source, defines, output):
    glslc = shutil.which("glslc")
    if glslc:
        command = [glslc, "-O", "--target-env=vulkan1.0"] + ["-D" + define for define in defines] + [source, "-o", output]
        subprocess.check_call(command)
        return

    validator = shutil.which("glslangValidator")
    if not validator:
        sys.exit("neither glslc nor glslangValidator was found")

    command = [validator, "-V", "--target-env", "vulkan1.0", "--quiet"] + ["-D" + define for define in defines] + [source, "-o", output]
    subprocess.check_call(command)

    optimiser = shutil.which("spirv-opt")
    if optimiser:
        subprocess.check_call([optimiser, "-O", "--target-env=vulkan1.0", output, "-o", output])


def convert_stage(file, name, defines):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
        output = os.path.join(directory, "stage.spv")
        compile_stage(os.path.join(SHADER_DIRECTORY, file), defines, output)

        validator = shutil.which("spirv-val")
        if validator:
            subprocess.check_call([validator, "--target-env", "vulkan1.0", output])

        with open(output, "rb") as stream:
            data = stream.read()

    if len(data) % 4 != 0:
        sys.exit("%s: SPIR-V length is not a multiple of 4" % file)

    words = struct.unpack("<%dI" % (len(data) // 4), data)
    lines = ["\tinline constexpr uint32_t %s[] = {" % name]
    for index in range(0, len(words), WORDS_PER_LINE):
        lines.append("\t\t" + ", ".join("0x%08xu" % word for word in words[index:index + WORDS_PER_LINE]) + ",")
    lines.append("\t};")
    lines.append("")

    print("%-44s %6d bytes, %d words" % (name, len(data), len(words)))
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main():
    body = "".join(convert_stage(*stage) for stage in STAGES)
    with open(OUTPUT_FILE, "w", newline="\n") as stream:
        stream.write(HEADER + "\n" + body + "}\n")
    print("wrote " + OUTPUT_FILE)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

`shaders/composite.frag`:

```frag
/*
 * scvk - a native Vulkan renderer for SimCity 4
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 aspctt
 *
 * This library is free software; you can redistribute it and/or
 * modify it under the terms of the GNU Lesser General Public
 * License as published by the Free Software Foundation, under
 * version 2.1 of the License, or (at your option) any later version.
 *
 * This library is distributed in the hope that it will be useful,
 * but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
 * MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.  See the GNU
 * Lesser General Public License for more details.
 *
 * You should have received a copy of the GNU Lesser General Public
 * License along with this library; if not, see <https://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.
 */

/*
 * The shadow composite, SCD3D11's CompositePS: darkens the back buffer wherever the
 * scene depth lies in the shadow map's shadow or below the terrain's shadow ceiling.
 *
 * Each pixel's view position is rebuilt from the depth through the pass's own
 * projection. A shadow takes away the sun's direct light, so a face turned partly away
 * from the sun is darkened less and one turned fully away not at all; terrain pixels use
 * the vertex normals SimCity 4 lights the terrain with rather than their facets'.
 *
 * The depth is Direct3D's, 0 to 1, and the shadow map is laid out as SCD3D11's: the
 * caster pass flips y so that both read the same.
 */

#version 450

layout(set = 0, binding = 0, std140) uniform CompositeConstants
{
	mat4 lightMatrix;
	vec4 material;      // x: the depth bias in light space
	vec4 projection0;   // p[0], p[5], p[10], p[12]
	vec4 projection1;   // p[13], p[14], shadow map texel, opacity
	vec4 viewport;      // the pass's viewport: x, y, width, height, from the top left
	vec4 tone;          // the shadow colour
	vec4 sun;           // the direction light travels in view space; w: 1 / N.L of flat ground, 0 for all faces
	mat4 eyeToWorld;    // view space to world, for the terrain maps
	vec4 terrainAxes;   // world xz to the map's along (xy) and across (zw) axes
	vec4 terrainGrid;   // map uv = (along * x + y, across * z + w)
	vec4 terrainShade;  // terrain map on, bias, 1 / softness, shadow map on
	vec4 terrainCell;   // cell width, how close to the terrain a terrain pixel lies, vertices x, z
} constants;

layout(set = 0, binding = 1) uniform sampler2D sceneDepth;
layout(set = 0, binding = 2) uniform sampler2D shadowMap;
layout(set = 0, binding = 3) uniform sampler2D terrainCeiling;
layout(set = 0, binding = 4) uniform sampler2D terrainVertices; // altitude, normal x, normal z, cell flipped

layout(location = 0) out vec4 outColour;

float SceneDepth(ivec2 pixel)
{
	ivec2 size = textureSize(sceneDepth, 0);
	return texelFetch(sceneDepth, clamp(pixel, ivec2(0), size - 1), 0).r;
}

vec3 ViewPosition(ivec2 pixel, float depth)
{
	// A partial static pass renders its dirty rectangle through a projection fitted to
	// that rectangle, so NDC spans the viewport, not the window.
	vec2  uv   = (vec2(pixel) + 0.5 - constants.viewport.xy) / constants.viewport.zw;
	float ndcX = uv.x * 2.0 - 1.0;
	float ndcY = 1.0 - uv.y * 2.0;

	vec3 viewPosition;
	viewPosition.x = (ndcX - constants.projection0.w) / constants.projection0.x;
	viewPosition.y = (ndcY - constants.projection1.x) / constants.projection0.y;
	viewPosition.z = (depth * 2.0 - 1.0 - constants.projection1.y) / constants.projection0.z;
	return viewPosition;
}

// Of the two neighbours along one axis, the one on the same surface: the smaller depth
// step. Keeps silhouette edges from bending the normal.
vec3 SurfaceStep(ivec2 pixel, vec3 centre, ivec2 axis)
{
	vec3 forward  = ViewPosition(pixel + axis, SceneDepth(pixel + axis)) - centre;
	vec3 backward = centre - ViewPosition(pixel - axis, SceneDepth(pixel - axis));
	return (abs(forward.z) < abs(backward.z)) ? forward : backward;
}

vec4 TerrainVertex(ivec2 cell)
{
	return texelFetch(terrainVertices, cell, 0);
}

// The terrain under a world position as SimCity 4 draws it: the cell's two triangles,
// split along the diagonal its flip flag picks, with the vertex normals its lighting uses
// interpolated across them. Returns the altitude.
float TerrainSurface(vec2 xz, out vec3 normal)
{
	vec2  grid = xz / constants.terrainCell.x;
	ivec2 cell = clamp(ivec2(floor(grid)), ivec2(0), ivec2(constants.terrainCell.zw) - 2);
	vec2  f    = clamp(grid - vec2(cell), 0.0, 1.0);

	vec4 v00 = TerrainVertex(cell);
	vec4 v10 = TerrainVertex(cell + ivec2(1, 0));
	vec4 v01 = TerrainVertex(cell + ivec2(0, 1));
	vec4 v11 = TerrainVertex(cell + ivec2(1, 1));

	vec4 v;
	if (v00.w != 0.0)
	{
		v = (f.x + f.y <= 1.0) ? v00 * (1.0 - f.x - f.y) + v10 * f.x + v01 * f.y
		                       : v11 * (f.x + f.y - 1.0) + v01 * (1.0 - f.x) + v10 * (1.0 - f.y);
	}
	else
	{
		v = (f.x >= f.y) ? v00 * (1.0 - f.x) + v10 * (f.x - f.y) + v11 * f.y
		                 : v00 * (1.0 - f.y) + v01 * (f.y - f.x) + v11 * f.x;
	}

	normal = normalize(vec3(v.y, sqrt(clamp(1.0 - v.y * v.y - v.z * v.z, 0.0, 1.0)), v.z));
	return v.x;
}

// The ceiling filtered bilinearly and clamped to its edge, worked out here because linear
// filtering of 32-bit float images is not something every device offers.
float TerrainCeiling(vec2 uv)
{
	ivec2 size   = textureSize(terrainCeiling, 0);
	vec2  texel  = uv * vec2(size) - 0.5;
	ivec2 origin = ivec2(floor(texel));
	vec2  f      = texel - vec2(origin);

	ivec2 last = size - 1;
	float c00 = texelFetch(terrainCeiling, clamp(origin, ivec2(0), last), 0).r;
	float c10 = texelFetch(terrainCeiling, clamp(origin + ivec2(1, 0), ivec2(0), last), 0).r;
	float c01 = texelFetch(terrainCeiling, clamp(origin + ivec2(0, 1), ivec2(0), last), 0).r;
	float c11 = texelFetch(terrainCeiling, clamp(origin + ivec2(1, 1), ivec2(0), last), 0).r;

	return mix(mix(c00, c10, f.x), mix(c01, c11, f.x), f.y);
}

void main()
{
	ivec2 pixel = ivec2(gl_FragCoord.xy);
	float depth = SceneDepth(pixel);

	if (depth >= 0.999999)
	{
		discard;
	}

	vec3 viewPosition = ViewPosition(pixel, depth);
	bool isTerrainMapUsed = constants.terrainShade.x != 0.0;
	vec3 world = isTerrainMapUsed ? (constants.eyeToWorld * vec4(viewPosition, 1.0)).xyz : vec3(0.0);

	// Beyond the city's edge lies the game's backdrop, below the terrain and so under its
	// shadow ceiling. Nothing out there casts, and shading it only leaves patches where
	// edge strips are redrawn without the composite.
	vec2 cityExtent = (constants.terrainCell.zw - 1.0) * constants.terrainCell.x;
	if (isTerrainMapUsed && (any(lessThan(world.xz, vec2(-1.0))) || any(greaterThan(world.xz, cityExtent + 1.0))))
	{
		discard;
	}

	// The surface's normal, rebuilt from the neighbouring depths, facing the camera
	vec3 surfaceNormal = normalize(cross(SurfaceStep(pixel, viewPosition, ivec2(0, 1)), SurfaceStep(pixel, viewPosition, ivec2(1, 0))));
	if (surfaceNormal.z < 0.0)
	{
		surfaceNormal = -surfaceNormal;
	}

	// Darken fully where N.L is that of flat ground, what SimCity 4's shadow strength is
	// set for, less on a face turned partly away, and not at all on one turned fully away
	float facing = 1.0;

	if (constants.sun.w != 0.0)
	{
		vec3 normal = surfaceNormal;

		float light = dot(normal, -constants.sun.xyz);

		if (isTerrainMapUsed)
		{
			vec3  vertexNormal;
			float ground      = TerrainSurface(world.xz, vertexNormal);
			mat3  toWorld     = mat3(constants.eyeToWorld);
			vec3  worldNormal = toWorld * normal;

			if (abs(world.y - ground) < constants.terrainCell.y && worldNormal.y > 0.3 * length(worldNormal))
			{
				light = dot(vertexNormal, -normalize(toWorld * constants.sun.xyz));
			}
		}

		facing = clamp(light * constants.sun.w, 0.0, 1.0);
		if (facing < 0.001)
		{
			discard;
		}
	}

	// The casters' shadow, filtered over the nine texels around the pixel's
	float shade = 0.0;

	if (constants.terrainShade.w != 0.0)
	{
		// Look the shadow up from just off the surface, along its normal
		//
		// A caster is also a receiver: a raised road deck or a ramp lies in the shadow
		// map as well as on screen, and compared with its own depth, rounded to texels
		// a few metres wide, it shadowed itself in bands on the side facing the sun.
		// Pushing the lookup out by one and a half texels, the reach of the 3x3 filter,
		// keeps every sample off the surface the pixel is on, while a real caster above
		// it still covers it. One texel is 2 / size in the light's clip space, which the
		// light matrix's first row scales from view space.
		float texelWorld = 2.0 * constants.projection1.z / length(vec3(constants.lightMatrix[0][0], constants.lightMatrix[1][0], constants.lightMatrix[2][0]));
		vec3  lookup     = viewPosition + surfaceNormal * (1.5 * texelWorld);

		vec4 light    = constants.lightMatrix * vec4(lookup, 1.0);
		vec2 shadowUV = light.xy * vec2(0.5, -0.5) + 0.5;

		if (all(greaterThanEqual(shadowUV, vec2(0.0))) && all(lessThanEqual(shadowUV, vec2(1.0))) && light.z >= 0.0 && light.z <= 1.0)
		{
			for (int y = -1; y <= 1; y++)
			{
				for (int x = -1; x <= 1; x++)
				{
					float caster = textureLod(shadowMap, shadowUV + vec2(x, y) * constants.projection1.z, 0.0).r;
					shade += (light.z > caster + constants.material.x) ? 1.0 : 0.0;
				}
			}

			shade /= 9.0;
		}
	}

	// The terrain's own shadow: a point below the ceiling the map holds for its (x, z).
	// The larger of the two shadows wins, so they never stack.
	if (isTerrainMapUsed)
	{
		vec2  axes    = vec2(dot(world.xz, constants.terrainAxes.xy), dot(world.xz, constants.terrainAxes.zw));
		float ceiling = TerrainCeiling(axes * constants.terrainGrid.xz + constants.terrainGrid.yw);
		shade = max(shade, clamp((ceiling - world.y - constants.terrainShade.y) * constants.terrainShade.z, 0.0, 1.0));
	}

	shade *= facing;
	if (shade < 0.001)
	{
		discard;
	}

	outColour = vec4(constants.tone.rgb, shade * constants.projection1.w);
}

/*
 * One triangle covering the viewport, for the passes that work per pixel of the back
 * buffer. They read gl_FragCoord rather than any coordinate passed down.
 */

#version 450

void main()
{
	vec2 corner = vec2((gl_VertexIndex << 1) & 2, gl_VertexIndex & 2);
	gl_Position = vec4(corner * 2.0 - 1.0, 0.0, 1.0);
